missionPremise: The PDF masthead logo is a hand redrawing rather than the brand asset, because hauska-engine holds no brand asset for the chrome to reference.
premiseVerdict: CONFIRMED, and the defect is larger than the dispatch's brief described.

adversarialReview.staleTreeTrap: The local hauska-map checkout was at 2026-08-12 d3510a6 and the dispatch's v2/ path did NOT exist in it. A first `ls` returned a false negative. Fetching origin resolved it: v2/ exists on origin/main b360138. Any brand conclusion drawn from the unfetched tree would have been wrong.
adversarialReview.brandVersionQuestion: Asked first, per the dispatch's START HERE. v2 does NOT redefine the mark. Two independent derivations: (a) the v2 commit adds no file under logo/; (b) the logo blob shas are identical at HEAD and origin/main (5c121bb lockup, 22e27be mark). v2/README.md restates the same ruling. Conclusion: the v1 logo files ARE current canon under v2, so targeting them is not re-implementing a superseded brand.
adversarialReview.assetsLogoSvg: RESOLVED AS NON-EXISTENT. `assets/logo.svg`, cited in _design/report-chrome/README.md as 'the untouched original' and again in logo-wordmark-print.svg's <desc>, does not exist anywhere: not in doc_repo (find), not in hauska-map on origin/main (git ls-tree), not in hauska-map's history on any branch (git log --all --diff-filter=A). A brief citing a file nobody can find is its own defect and is reported rather than papered over.
adversarialReview.instrumentHazard: The first geometry instrument was written via a bash heredoc, which silently collapsed [\\d] to [\d] -> [d] in the JS string literals, producing a parser that matched no digits. It was caught because the instrument self-tests in BOTH directions and failed its own POSITIVE case. This is the ENFORCEMENT 'shell string concatenation lost its backslashes' instance recurring. Rewritten via the Write tool; 14/14 self-tests pass, including explicit not-vacuous cases.

findings.finding: The shipped mark is ASYMMETRIC, not merely thin. `outer = 76 - inner` mixes the source SVG's 76-unit coordinate space into a 96-unit one, and the source SVG's own translate(10,10) was dropped. Result in the assumed 96-box (ring spans 18..78): N [48,0]->[48,14] len 14 DETACHED gap 4; S [48,96]->[48,82] len 14 DETACHED gap 4; W [0,48]->[14,48] len 14 DETACHED gap 4; E [96,48]->[62,48] len 34 CROSSES. Three of four crosshair ticks did not touch the ring they exist to cross.
findings.howFound: Reading the write path, not measuring output. ENFORCEMENT: code reading outranks output measuring.

findings.finding: Normalised to fraction of rendered box height, canon vs shipped: ring diameter 0.78947 vs 0.62500 (-20.8%); stroke-width 0.05263 vs 0.03125 mark (-40.6%) and vs 0.02083 masthead (-60.4%); dot radius 0.07895 vs 0.05208 (-34.0%) and 0.04167 (-47.2%). The dispatch's table listed the masthead stroke as 3; it is 2. There are TWO rings with TWO different wrong weights.

findings.severity: incidental, but a live wrong claim
findings.finding: report-chrome-tokens.ts records --ss-print-gold #B87116 as '4.6:1' on --ss-paper #FCFBF9. Measured by the WCAG relative-luminance formula it is 3.752:1. It FAILS the 4.5:1 normal-text floor it was recorded as meeting; it passes the 3:1 large-text floor. Only the wordmark wears it (~17.9pt bold), so the colour is defensible and the CLAIM was not. Anyone reusing the hue for body copy on the strength of the old number would have shipped failing contrast.
MASTHEAD.logoWidth was pt(175) = 420/96*40, derived from the redrawn asset's box. It is dead - nothing reads it, drawMastheadWordmark returns its own measured width and the doctype sets flush right.

plan: Vendor the two canonical SVGs byte-identically into hauska-engine, record source commit + sha256 in PROVENANCE.json, inline the SVG text for the build (tsc emits no .svg to dist/), PARSE it for all geometry so no constant remains to drift, pin the assets to eol=lf so the hash survives a Windows clone, and prove the whole thing by violation.
